primary_methods.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
primary_methods.takeaway: PCGrad changes individual task loss gradients only for negative pairwise products, repeats projections in random task order, sums modified gradients and supplies the result to a gradient optimizer. It explicitly applies to shared parameters; negative conflicts alone are not necessarily detrimental.
primary_methods.candidate_difference: Current graph-weighted member-minus-pool logit response constraints operate on one actual native shared displacement, preserving its pooled directional effect. Neither the protected functional nor the post-optimizer moment convention equals member-task PCGrad.
primary_methods.remaining_qualification: v1 printed pseudocode was read; author code/latest v4 and source-specific gradient normalization, coupled closures and optimizer integration remain unqualified.

primary_methods.title: Orthogonal Gradient Descent for Continual Learning
primary_methods.takeaway: OGD stores previous-task logit-gradient directions, projects new-task loss updates away from their span and preserves prior outputs locally. Ground-truth-logit/subset variants reduce storage. It distinguishes model-output gradients from loss gradients and relies on a locality approximation for stored directions.
primary_methods.candidate_difference: Refreshes graph-weighted current member-minus-pool margin response gradients, uses one-sided constraints and pooled-progress equality, and does not claim past-task/full-output invariance. This is the closest consulted response-preserving projection operator.
primary_methods.qualification_caution: High parameter dimension does not guarantee feasible contrast protection once pooled-neutral and correction-size constraints are imposed. No source theorem is transferred to shared-body AdamW.
